topic: Quotient-tangent efficiency for nonunique proximal ATE bridges. Work in the dominated observed-data proximal model for O=(Y,A,Z,W,X) whose only bridge restrictions are existence of square-integrable outcome and treatment bridges; neither bridge is unique. Restrict to locally constant closed-range/rank strata and require pathwise differentiability, but do not add bijectivity, surjectivity, or a preferred minimum-norm bridge as a model assumption. Characterize the tangent space and prove an iff criterion for ATE pathwise differentiability. Define the proximal bridge-quotient canonical gradient as the minimum-norm element of the closed affine hull of all valid bridge doubly-robust scores, enlarged if tangent completeness requires it. Prove its efficiency bound and construct a cross-fitted penalized-minimax/Galerkin affine-ensemble one-step estimator with asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent variance estimation, and Wald coverage under explicit approximation and product-remainder conditions. The hard kernel is the general score-lifting/tangent-normal completeness theorem; a finite constrained-GMM calculation is only a witness. Anchor at Bennett et al. 2023/JRSS-B 2026 Theorems 3 and 6 plus their efficiency boundary, Zhang et al. 2023 Theorem 2.5, Imbens et al. 2025 Theorem 7, and Ai–Shan 2025; distinguish all uniqueness-restricted efficiency results. Cui et al.'s SUPPORT right-heart-catheterization analysis is the consumer: the theorem determines whether bridge-dependent standard errors are globally efficient under redundant proxies and supplies the variance-minimizing replacement. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normal generators and showed their closed span equals differences of bridge DR scores. An exact positive 36-cell example with both bridges nonunique has canonical variance 773723312/334026875, and an exact coefficient obstruction shows no single bridge pair attains it. A singular 3-by-3 branch example and four-corner affine-score identities were also checked. Destructive checks covered rank-changing neighborhoods, compact-operator closed-range collapse, Galerkin overclaims, product integrability, and current proximal-efficiency papers; no exact collision was found, but Bennett's final publisher text remains to be checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that scores of actual dominated paths span exactly the annihilator of the three normal classes across the accepted closed-range model, including moving kernels and the arms' shared marginal. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce both finite witnesses, then compare actual tangent-score spans with the proposed normal annihilator in positive 4-by-4 rank-two models with different arm row spaces; an extra unresolved normal direction requires revision. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_proximal_quotient_efficiency.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the observed-data tangent space of the proximal ATE model defined jointly by existence of square-integrable outcome and treatment bridges when both solution sets are non-singleton, and determine exactly when the ATE is pathwise differentiable.

source_refs.claim: The paper permits nonunique primal and debiasing solutions and proves root-n inference, but states that semiparametric efficiency is unclear when both are nonunique because variance depends on the selected pair.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney K. Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Propositions 2.3 and 2.5 characterize identified linear functionals by orthogonality to bridge-operator kernels, while Lemmas 2.4 and 2.6 connect root-n estimability to the corresponding adjoint ranges.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3 derives a generalized-inverse efficient influence function without Cui's surjectivity restrictions, but for a statistical model characterized by the outcome-bridge moment alone rather than joint existence of both proximal bridges.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: The unrestricted-bridge efficiency calculation is evaluated where both bridges are uniquely defined and the two conditional-expectation operators are surjective.
source_refs.author: Yifan Cui, Hongming Pu, Xu Shi, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest efficiency result, Chen and Xie, treats the observable model generated by one outcome-bridge conditional moment. Simultaneous existence of outcome and treatment bridges instead defines an intersection model with extra compatibility restrictions through their shared treatment-covariate marginal. Bennett et al. establish mixed-bias scores and inference for selected nonunique solutions but leave their global efficiency meaning unresolved. No cited result proves that scores of actual dominated paths exhaust the annihilator of the outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and null-space-interaction normals when both operator kernels may move along a path.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem identifying the closed tangent space as the annihilator of explicit joint bridge-solvability normal classes and equating ATE pathwise differentiability with existence of a square-integrable continuous derivative on the quotient tangent space.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from strong identifying assumptions to the observable statistical model, local overidentification, and the efficiency consequences of unused moment restrictions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy assumptions induce observable inverse-problem restrictions -> those restrictions may locally overidentify the observed law -> tangent-space analysis reveals efficiency gains -> the unresolved destination is the joint two-bridge existence model with nonunique solution sets

method_exemplars.technique: Translate conditional-moment restrictions into a score-range characterization and prove local overidentification through the closure of the derivative range and the kernel of its adjoint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired tangent-completeness theorem is a coupled, multi-restriction version of their range-versus-annihilator argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonalize sequential unconditional and conditional moments, minimize information over nuisance directions, and construct optimally weighted sieve estimators attaining the resulting bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Joint bridge existence produces coupled sequential moment restrictions, making their information-minimization machinery a close route to an attaining estimator once tangent completeness is established.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a bridge solution set, select a stable representative by an extremum criterion, and debias the target estimator using an adjoint representer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly handles nonunique proximal bridges; the required advance replaces representative selection with the joint-model quotient derivative.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the proximal bridge-quotient canonical gradient as the minimum-variance element generated by all valid outcome-treatment bridge doubly robust scores, and characterize when any single bridge pair attains that minimum.

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3 shows that the doubly robust representation is valid for every primal-dual solution pair, but the paper notes that pair-dependent variance has no established interpretation as a best-achievable variance under nonuniqueness.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney K. Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3 uses a generalized inverse to obtain the efficient influence function for a one-outcome-bridge negative-control model and recovers Cui's score only in the bijective case.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: The familiar proximal doubly robust expression is established as the efficient influence function on a uniqueness-and-surjectivity submodel, although it remains an unbiased estimating function without bridge uniqueness.
source_refs.author: Yifan Cui, Hongming Pu, Xu Shi, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper derives efficiency bounds for identified linear functionals of an NPIV regression without requiring the regression function itself to be identified.
source_refs.author: Thomas A. Severini and Gautam Tripathi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cui et al. identify one bridge-pair score as efficient only after uniqueness and surjectivity collapse both solution sets. Bennett et al. show that every valid pair gives a doubly robust score but explicitly leave the pair-dependent variances without a global efficiency interpretation. Chen and Xie's generalized-inverse projection resolves the nearest one-bridge model, not the smaller model in which both bridge equations must remain solvable. The missing object is the projection geometry of the complete affine family of bridge-pair scores, possibly enlarged by gradient directions not representable by one pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A projection formula for the unique minimum-norm canonical gradient in the closed affine hull of valid bridge doubly robust scores, together with necessary and sufficient equations for single-pair attainment and an explicit variance-gap formula otherwise.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the central paradox: the causal functional can be strongly identified while nuisance solutions are weakly identified and nonunique, yet the inferential score depends on the solutions selected by regularization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional moments admit many nuisance solutions -> the target remains root-n estimable through a dual representer -> every solution pair yields a valid doubly robust score -> seek the globally variance-minimizing quotient score rather than a regularization-selected score

method_exemplars.technique: Express the efficient influence function through a generalized inverse of an information operator obtained by minimizing over conditional-moment nuisance directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its generalized-inverse influence function is the nearest existing projection formula, but the desired object must incorporate both existential bridge restrictions and their interaction.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent an identified functional on an underidentified inverse-problem quotient and calculate its efficiency bound without selecting an identified structural function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proximal ATE is likewise invariant over bridge null spaces, with the new difficulty of two coupled inverse problems.

method_exemplars.technique: Use penalized minimax estimation to stabilize nonunique primal and dual nuisances, then cross-fit their doubly robust score to obtain asymptotic linearity and studentized inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an implementable estimator for individual affine-family members; a quotient-efficient procedure must retain this stability while estimating the variance-minimizing combination.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a feasible cross-fitted affine-ensemble estimator that attains the joint nonunique-bridge efficiency bound while allowing penalized-minimax or Galerkin approximations of both bridge solution sets.

source_refs.claim: Theorems 6 and 7 establish asymptotic linearity, normality, consistent variance estimation, and Wald coverage for a cross-fitted penalized-minimax score based on fixed regularization-selected nuisance limits, but not global efficiency under nonuniqueness.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney K. Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper estimates a nonunique proximal solution set, selects a uniquely defined representative, and proves that a debiased counterfactual-mean estimator is root-n regular and locally efficient under additional conditions.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: The paper jointly estimates a parametrically indexed outcome bridge and the ATE with increasing moment restrictions and obtains efficiency in a submodel where the bridge parameter is uniquely determined.
source_refs.author: Chunrong Ai and Jiawei Shan

source_refs.claim: The paper proposes optimally weighted minimum-distance and influence-function implementations for its one-bridge generalized-inverse efficiency bound, leaving the joint two-bridge affine ensemble untreated.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Haitian Xie

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing procedures resolve nonuniqueness by selecting one stable representative, impose a finite-dimensional uniquely determined bridge, or estimate the efficient score of a one-bridge model. None estimates projection coefficients over the affine family of all valid proximal bridge-pair scores while controlling inverse-problem first-stage error. The asymptotic expansion must therefore add control of the estimated score-affine subspace and its minimum-norm projection, including Galerkin approximation bias, empirical Gram-operator instability, and the usual primal-dual product remainder.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cross-fitted one-step estimator with an explicit penalized-minimax or Galerkin affine-ensemble construction, an asymptotic-linear expansion in the quotient canonical gradient, ratio-consistent variance estimation, and valid Wald coverage under stated approximation, conditioning, and product-remainder rates.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates efficiency losses through inefficient bridge estimation and failure to account for correlations among estimation steps, then connects the proposed improvement to the SUPPORT application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bridge inversion is statistically difficult -> sequential plug-in estimation discards covariance information -> joint moment estimation can lower variance -> extend joint optimization to affine score classes when neither bridge is unique

method_exemplars.technique: Penalized-minimax nuisance estimation with cross-fitting, a mixed-bias expansion, critical-radius and approximation-error control, consistent empirical variance, and Wald inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator has the same nonunique inverse-problem nuisances and product remainders but must additionally estimate the optimal affine-score projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Use iterated Tikhonov adversarial estimation and source-condition double robustness to obtain asymptotic normality when either the primal or dual inverse problem is sufficiently well posed.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its source-condition analysis supplies explicit rate conditions for the two ill-posed bridge equations before the affine ensemble is formed.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate an efficient NPIV functional with an orthogonalized, optimally weighted sieve minimum-distance score and prove root-n asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The affine projection is an optimally weighted inverse-problem functional, so their sieve weighting argument gives a concrete route from population projection to a feasible attaining estimator.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the loss of regularity and attainable inference for the proximal ATE along local sequences approaching a bridge-operator rank or closed-range boundary from constant-rank nonunique strata.

source_refs.claim: The paper separates strong identification of a functional from weak identification and ill-posedness of its nuisance solution, but its normality results impose pointwise rate and approximation conditions rather than a local-to-rank-change analysis.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney K. Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains strong L2 rates for fixed inverse-problem solutions without uniqueness or closedness using source conditions, underscoring the sharp interaction between range conditions and statistical regularity.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney K. Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: The paper gives pointwise range conditions for root-n estimation and a regular estimator under additional assumptions, but does not characterize local sequences on which the relevant range or kernel changes.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Local overidentification is linked to proper tangent-space restrictions and efficiency gains at a fixed law, but the framework does not supply uniform proximal inference across changing operator ranks.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Andres Santos

open_problems.why_unsolved: Constant-rank and closed-range assumptions can make quotient projections well behaved at a fixed law, yet an arbitrarily nearby distribution may gain or lose bridge-null directions or lose closed range. The canonical-gradient norm, affine projection, or pathwise differentiability can then change discontinuously. Existing proximal and inverse-problem papers provide pointwise regularity under source or range conditions but do not locate the local asymptotic transition or determine whether nominal Wald intervals remain honest near rank boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic minimax or impossibility theorem describing the canonical-variance and convergence-rate transition under singular-value sequences approaching zero, together with a uniformly valid regularized confidence procedure on the largest admissible neighborhood class.

writing_exemplar.why: Its strong-functional versus weak-nuisance distinction cleanly motivates separating point identification, root-n regularity, and inverse-problem conditioning.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bridge functions may be weakly identified -> a functional can nevertheless be pointwise root-n estimable -> source and approximation conditions control pointwise inference -> determine honest behavior near a rank-changing nonregular boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze constrained penalized-minimax inverse regression through source conditions without uniqueness or closedness and derive strong-metric error bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its singular-value and source-condition machinery can parameterize proximity to the rank boundary and control regularized bridge estimation along local sequences.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate finiteness of an efficiency bound for an underidentified inverse-problem functional to an adjoint-range condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase transition occurs when the proximal ATE derivative approaches or exits the relevant adjoint range.

method_exemplars.technique: Use iterated Tikhonov regularization and source-condition double robustness to trade inverse-problem bias against variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniformly valid inference near a rank boundary requires this explicit bias-variance accounting, augmented by local-sequence lower bounds.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop an estimable diagnostic for whether the bridge pair used in the SUPPORT right-heart-catheterization analysis produces the globally efficient score under proxy redundancy, and a variance-minimizing replacement when it does not.

source_refs.claim: The paper applies a bridge-dependent proximal doubly robust estimator to 5,735 SUPPORT patients and interprets its score as efficient on the uniqueness-and-surjectivity submodel.
source_refs.author: Yifan Cui, Hongming Pu, Xu Shi, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper revisits SUPPORT with increasing-moment joint GMM and shows possible efficiency gains over plug-in or usual doubly robust procedures, but assumes a uniquely determined finite-dimensional bridge parameter.
source_refs.author: Chunrong Ai and Jiawei Shan

source_refs.claim: The paper links local overidentification to efficiency gains and nontrivial specification testing and constructs Hausman-style diagnostics in related conditional-moment causal models.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: The paper proves that local overidentification is equivalent to more efficient estimation of some smooth parameters and to specification tests with nontrivial local power.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen and Andres Santos

open_problems.why_unsolved: The SUPPORT standard error in Cui et al. is tied to a fitted bridge pair whose global optimality follows only under uniqueness and surjectivity. Ai and Shan show possible efficiency gains in the same data but derive them in a uniquely parameterized bridge submodel, so those gains do not isolate the information supplied by redundant valid proxies in the nonparametric joint-existence model. No cited procedure estimates the residual between a fitted bridge score and the joint-model quotient projection or tests the single-pair attainment condition while accounting for inverse-problem first-stage error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A consistent estimator of the bridge-score efficiency gap and a Hausman- or projection-residual test with a stated null and local-alternative limit law, coupled to an affine-ensemble one-step estimator and valid standard error when the null is rejected.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the substantive proxy construction, clinical estimand, and benchmark analysis that the diagnostic would revisit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unmeasured severity threatens the RHC comparison -> treatment- and outcome-inducing proxies identify the 30-day survival effect -> a bridge-pair DR estimator supplies a standard error -> determine whether that standard error is globally efficient with redundant proxies

method_exemplars.technique: Construct Hausman and incremental-moment tests from tangent-space overidentifying restrictions and derive nontrivial local power.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed diagnostic tests whether unused bridge-score directions contain variance-reducing information, the proximal analogue of their local-overidentification tests.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate a conditional bridge restriction by increasing unconditional moments, jointly estimate the bridge and ATE, select sieve dimension by estimated MSE, and estimate the resulting variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is already implemented on SUPPORT and uses covariance among bridge and target moments to reduce variance; the required change is optimization over bridge equivalence classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Stabilize nonunique bridge estimates with penalized-minimax criteria and use cross-fitted scores for consistent studentization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both the diagnostic and replacement estimator require stable nuisance limits without elevating a minimum-norm bridge to a scientific model assumption.

literature_map:
Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Biometrika, doi:10.1093/biomet/asy038) establish proximal ATE identification through outcome bridges and note that the causal functional can be invariant across bridge solutions.
Cui et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2011.08411, doi:10.1080/01621459.2023.2191817) derive the familiar proximal DR score and efficiency bound on a submodel with unique bridges and surjective conditional-expectation operators; their SUPPORT analysis is the application anchor.
Zhang et al. (2023, Statistics & Probability Letters, arXiv:2303.10134, doi:10.1016/j.spl.2023.109836) directly treat nonunique proximal bridges, characterize identified functionals by kernel orthogonality, and connect root-n estimability to a dual bridge/range condition.
Bennett et al. (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2208.08291, doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf075) prove mixed-bias identities and cross-fitted penalized-minimax inference for strongly identified functionals of nonunique nuisance solutions.
The decisive Bennett boundary is explicit: when primal and dual solutions are both nonunique, variance depends on the selected pair and its status as the global semiparametric efficiency bound is unclear.
Chen and Xie (2026, Cowles DP 2497, arXiv:2510.16683) are the closest collision: Theorem 3 gives a generalized-inverse influence function for a nonunique outcome-bridge negative-control model and shows Cui's score can be inefficient outside the bijective case.
Chen and Xie do not settle the requested joint model: their statistical model is characterized by the outcome-bridge moment alone, and their long-term-model efficiency analysis explicitly omits the second bridge.
Imbens et al. (2025, JRSSB, arXiv:2202.07234, doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkae095) prove doubly robust inference and efficiency only with unique bridges and a bijective operator; their Remark 5 identifies redundant proxy categories as a source of nonuniqueness.
Ai and Shan (2025, Statistica Sinica, arXiv:2501.02214) use increasing-moment joint GMM and revisit SUPPORT, but assume a uniquely determined finite-dimensional outcome-bridge parameter for their efficiency comparison.
Ai and Chen (2012, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2012.05.015) provide information-minimization and optimally weighted sieve machinery for sequential conditional moments with unknown functions.
Severini and Tripathi (2012, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2012.05.018) derive efficiency bounds for identified linear functionals of underidentified NPIV regressions, supplying the closest quotient-functional precedent.
Chen and Santos (2018, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA13559) connect tangent-range deficits, local overidentification, efficiency gains, and nontrivial specification tests.
Bennett et al. (2023, COLT, arXiv:2302.05404) and Bennett et al. (2023, arXiv:2307.13793) supply penalized-minimax and iterated-Tikhonov tools for nonunique ill-posed inverse problems, but not the joint proximal quotient gradient.
The surviving gap is narrower than generic efficiency without uniqueness: it comprises tangent-normal completeness, canonical affine-score projection, feasible attaining inference, rank-boundary behavior, and an application-facing efficiency diagnostic for the intersection of two existential nonunique proximal bridge restrictions.
